$comment: Single source of truth for scope (Lesson 8). Every feature carries the triple: behavior + verification + state, plus evidence. Only the checker/verification script flips status to passing/done (Lesson 9). attempts/maxAttempts is a timebox: the maker increments attempts on every iteration it works a feature and MUST set status=blocked (with a reason in checkerNotes) once attempts reaches maxAttempts, instead of continuing to retry indefinitely. `context` is the handoff INTO implementation: the 1-3 files the feature touches, plus one line the implementer would otherwise rediscover. `evidence` is a LIST OF RUNS, not a paragraph: [{date, run: red|green, cmd, result}]. `behavior` and `falsifier` are ONE SENTENCE each. Each feature also carries kind (build|prove) and falsifier: the specific wrong implementation its verification would fail on, citing an `[INV-AREA-N]` id from docs/design/runtime-model.md or docs/design/tool-surface.md wherever one exists (docs/reference/invariant-contract.md). Cut 2026-08-20 from the approved design (loop/design-approval.json digest c0a83df4b8d6c5b2): 10 named components, build order per docs/design/tool-surface.md#Build-order (file-sync-watcher + readiness-gate before any capability tool; code actions last), enforced here as real dependency edges, not just prose.

TCON-ROUTE-0001 declares technique `decision_table` (row per combination) but has no row for the ancestor-pom-without-<modules> combination. The oracle layer should add that row (parent-only root pom with <packaging>pom</packaging> and no <modules>, an independent child project with its own pom beneath it: the child path must resolve to the CHILD, not the root). This sharpens the risk the human already accepted in design-approval 3d68e0857fbfac45 — that approval says <modules> detection 'is validated only against the current fixture tree', but the probe shows the current fixture tree validates it not at all. features.name: Prove: routing never drifts and never silently misroutes
features.behavior: Over a fixture tree containing a single-module project, a multi-module reactor, a non-reactor parent pom.xml with an independently rooted nested child project, a reactor nested inside another reactor, and an unmanaged directory, every path resolves to its correct root (the outermost enclosing reactor root, nearest ancestor pom.xml, or an explicit unmanaged-path error), and distinct roots never collide

context.note: Build the fixture tree with a real multi-module pom.xml (<modules>), a plain single-module project, and an unmanaged path. Preserve TCON-ROUTE-0001..0004, TCON-ROUTE-0005 for the explicit named-path error required by INV-ROUTE-2, and TCON-ROUTE-0006 for the non-reactor-ancestor fallback required by INV-ROUTE-1. Add TCON-ROUTE-0007: reactor A declares <modules> at the fixture root, and nested inside one of A's module directories is reactor B, which independently declares its own <modules>; a path under one of B's modules must resolve to A (the outermost enclosing reactor), not B, discriminating the 'outermost' clause of INV-ROUTE-1 from an implementation that stops at the innermost or nearest enclosing reactor (mutant: `mavenRoots.find(...)` instead of `mavenRoots.findLast(...)`).

features.falsifier: a multi-module project resolves one workspace id per module instead of one at the reactor root [INV-ROUTE-3]; two calls under the same reactor root resolve to different workspace ids [INV-ROUTE-1][INV-ROUTE-3]; an unmanaged path returns an empty success or an error that does not name the path [INV-ROUTE-2]; a path beneath a non-reactor ancestor pom.xml (no <modules>) resolves to that ancestor instead of falling back to the path's own nearest ancestor pom.xml [INV-ROUTE-1]; or a path under a reactor nested inside another reactor (both declaring <modules>) resolves to the inner nested reactor instead of the outermost enclosing reactor [INV-ROUTE-1]

CHECKER VERDICT 2026-08-21 (attempt 3/3) — APPROVE. Chạy lại độc lập `npm run test:integration -- test/integration/project-router.integration.spec.ts`: 7/7 xanh (TCON-ROUTE-0001..0007), 179,6 ms, không có test fail/cancelled/skipped. Evidence của maker tái lập được nguyên văn.

Gap `outermost` do chính verdict 2/3 nêu ra đã đóng thật. Bằng chứng: probe mutant trong harness/trace/scratch/probe-route-0007 (bản sao scratch của src + spec, đã xóa sau khi dùng; src/ không bị chạm, `git diff --stat src/` rỗng). Control (bản sao chưa đột biến): 7/7 xanh, nên bản sao trung thực. M3 — đúng mutant từng sống sót 6/6 ở vòng trước, thay `mavenRoots.findLast(({ isReactor }) => isReactor)` bằng `mavenRoots.find(...)` — nay 6 pass / 1 fail, và TCON-ROUTE-0007 là điều kiện DUY NHẤT giết nó. Phân công giữa các điều kiện vẫn sạch: M1 (luôn lấy tổ tiên ngoài cùng, xóa kiểm tra <modules>) chỉ bị TCON-ROUTE-0006 giết; M2 (luôn lấy tổ tiên gần nhất) bị 0001, 0002, 0003, 0004, 0007 giết.

Quét mutant mở rộng để tránh lộ thêm gap ở vòng sau: M13 (băm workspaceId từ đối số thay vì projectRoot) bị 0001, 0002, 0003, 0004, 0007 giết; M14 (thông báo lỗi không nêu đường dẫn) bị 0005 giết; M17 (dừng đi ngược cây ở thư mục đầu tiên không có pom.xml) bị sáu điều kiện giết; M19 (bỏ nhánh dự phòng tổ tiên gần nhất) bị 0002, 0003, 0004, 0006 giết. Ba mutant sống sót: M12 (xem mục FOLLOW-UP ở trên, gap thật), M4 (nới regex thành /modules/i — rủi ro đã nhận trong design approval 3d68e0857fbfac45, do không dùng parser Maven model thật), M20 (bỏ nhánh statSync isDirectory) — M20 là mutant tương đương, vì `path.join(<đường dẫn tệp>, "pom.xml")` không bao giờ tồn tại và vòng lặp vẫn đi lên thư mục cha ngay sau đó. Mutant bỏ realpathSync cũng sống sót, nhưng spec ghi rõ ở đầu tệp rằng nó không khẳng định gì về phân giải symlink vì X-005 vẫn mở — đây là ranh giới phạm vi đã ghi, không phải gap ẩn.

TCON-ROUTE-0007 chưa từng đỏ khi test-implementer thêm vào, nên tự nó không chứng minh được gì; M3 mới là bằng chứng nó biết đỏ và đỏ đúng lý do. Không có lỗi R-T3: giá trị kỳ vọng `outerReactorRoot` lấy từ cấu trúc fixture và từ nguyên văn mệnh đề `outermost` của INV-ROUTE-1, không tái tạo cách code đi ngược cây thư mục. Không có lỗi R-T9: điều kiện sinh ra từ một mutant cụ thể và một mệnh đề spec, không phải từ các nhánh của implementation.

Behavior và falsifier sau khi mở rộng khớp với fixture và assertion thực tế. Fixture của TCON-ROUTE-0007 dựng reactor A khai báo <modules> ở gốc, reactor B lồng trong thư mục module của A và cũng khai báo <modules>, cùng một module con của riêng B. Ba hàng gọi (thư mục của B, thư mục module con của B, tệp nguồn trong module con) đều assert `projectRoot === outerReactorRoot`, `projectRoot !== innerReactorRoot`, và workspaceId bằng id của A. Có thêm tiền đề A tự phân giải về chính nó. Một điểm dùng từ chưa chặt, không chặn phê duyệt: behavior viết `over a fixture tree`, nhưng thực tế TCON-ROUTE-0005/0006/0007 mỗi điều kiện dựng cây tạm riêng, chỉ 0001..0004 dùng chung buildFixtureTree.

Diff của tệp oracle thuần cộng thêm (+64 dòng, không xóa dòng nào — đã kiểm chứng bằng `git diff | grep ^-`), nên không có assertion cũ nào bị nới lỏng. src/workspace/project-router.ts không đổi kể từ commit 2503299. ---------- lịch sử phía dưới ----------
FOLLOW-UP (ĐÃ ĐÓNG bởi TCON-ROUTE-0007, xác nhận ở verdict 3/3 phía trên): từ `outermost` trong INV-ROUTE-1 vẫn chưa được chứng minh bởi bất kỳ điều kiện nào, vì cây fixture không có reactor lồng trong reactor. features.behavior: The daemon listens on $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/jdt-mcp.sock under a single-instance lock so concurrent launches converge on one daemon process, and shutdown always terminates every JDT LS child it spawned

features.name: mcp-shim: stdio front end, connect-or-spawn
features.behavior: The shim connects to the daemon socket, auto-spawning the daemon under the lock when absent, copies newline-delimited MCP frames both ways, and never writes anything but a single valid MCP message to stdout

context.note: MCP stdio MUST NOT see embedded newlines and MUST see nothing on stdout but valid MCP messages (docs/design/evidence.md, spec quote) — every daemon log line, including errors during auto-spawn, goes to stderr or a file, never stdout.

features.name: diagnostics-cache: absorb publishDiagnostics
features.behavior: The cache stores the most recent publishDiagnostics payload per URI per workspace, with a later publish for the same URI fully replacing the earlier one rather than accumulating

context.note: Diagnostics arrive unsolicited, including for files never didOpen'ed (spike B, docs/design/evidence.md) — the cache must key by URI per workspace independent of any open/close lifecycle.

features.falsifier: publishing an empty diagnostics list for a URI leaves the previously-cached problems in place instead of fully replacing them [INV-DIAG-2]

features.name: java_diagnostics tool
features.behavior: java_diagnostics returns the cached problems for a file or an entire project, distinguishing an explicit 'not reported yet' marker from an empty (clean) result

context.note: This is item 4 in the build order specifically because its shape differs from the navigation tools — it reads a push cache, it never makes its own LSP request (docs/design/tool-surface.md#Build-order).

features.falsifier: a URI with no publish yet returns the same empty list as a URI JDT LS reported zero problems for, instead of a distinct 'not reported yet' marker [INV-DIAG-1]

features.name: Prove: diagnostics are never stale, never accumulated, never cross-workspace
features.behavior: Querying before and after the first publish for a file distinguishes not-reported from clean, publishing an empty list after a real one fully clears the cache, and two workspaces sharing the same relative path never serve each other's diagnostics

context.note: Reuse the spike-B two-workspace-same-relative-path fixture shape (docs/design/evidence.md) for the cross-workspace assertion — that is the exact scenario INV-DIAG-3 exists to forbid.

features.falsifier: a query before the first publish for a URI returns the same shape as a query after a clean publish [INV-DIAG-1]; or a publish-then-empty-publish sequence leaves stale problems cached [INV-DIAG-2]; or workspace B's cache serves a diagnostic published by workspace A for the same relative path [INV-DIAG-3]
features.checkerNotes:
BLOCKED: diagnostics oracle requires callable interfaces owned by two not-started dependencies.

TCON-DIAG-0001 through TCON-DIAG-0003 require real publishDiagnostics delivery and java_diagnostics queries through distinct live workspace instances. docs/design/tool-surface.md specifies arguments and observable semantics, but it does not define an executable/CLI entry point, TypeScript signature, notification-injection contract, or concrete not-reported result shape. feat-diagnostics-cache and feat-tool-diagnostics are both not-started, so writing the integration test now would invent their production interfaces or fail only on missing modules rather than behavior. Implement and specify those dependencies first, then route this proof feature back to test-implementer.

features.name: java_completion tool
features.behavior: java_completion returns completion items for path/line/column, capped and marked truncated:true with the true total when the cap is exceeded

context.note: Build-order item 5, chosen specifically because it is the high-volume result shape that stresses the cap (docs/design/tool-surface.md#Build-order) — depends on feat-prove-diagnostics finishing first per the design's explicit sequencing, not on any data dependency.

features.falsifier: a completion result in a large scope is returned uncapped instead of truncated:true plus the true total [INV-TOOL-3]

features.name: Prove: completion never returns an uncapped or silently-cut list
features.behavior: Requesting completion in a scope whose real item count exceeds the configured cap always returns truncated:true with the true total, never a silently shortened list and never the full uncapped set

context.note: Use a fixture class with more members than the configured cap so the scenario is exercised for real, not simulated with a mocked LSP response.

features.falsifier: a completion result whose real count exceeds the cap comes back without truncated:true, or with fewer items and no total, or with every item uncapped [INV-TOOL-3]
features.checkerNotes:
BLOCKED: completion oracle requires the callable interface owned by the not-started feat-tool-completion dependency.

The feature requires a real java_completion round trip against a fixture whose true item count exceeds the configured cap. docs/design/tool-surface.md specifies path/line/column arguments and the truncated:true plus true-total invariant, but it does not define an executable/CLI entry point, TypeScript signature, concrete completion item/result shape, or a way for the test to discover the configured cap. feat-tool-completion is not-started, so writing the integration test now would invent its production interface or fail only on a missing module rather than the required behavior. Implement and specify feat-tool-completion first, then route this proof feature back to test-implementer.

features.name: java_rename tool
features.behavior: java_rename returns the proposed multi-file WorkspaceEdit as data by default and only writes files to disk when the call carries apply:true

context.note: A-002/first mutating tool (docs/design/tool-surface.md#Build-order item 6) — a rename on the two-file fixture already produces a WorkspaceEdit touching two files (docs/design/evidence.md); apply must be opt-in per call, never a server-side default.

features.falsifier: a rename call with no apply argument writes the proposed edit to disk anyway, instead of returning it as data [INV-TOOL-2]

features.name: Prove: rename never writes without an explicit opt-in
features.behavior: A full sweep of rename calls with no apply argument leaves every file's mtime untouched, and a call with apply:true actually writes the proposed edit

context.note: Assert on real file mtimes across the fixture's whole tree, not just the target file — a daemon that writes an unrelated file behind an agent's back would still pass a target-file-only check.

features.falsifier: any file's mtime changes after a rename call with no apply argument [INV-TOOL-2]
features.checkerNotes: BLOCKED: The rename oracle cannot produce a behavioral red until dependency feat-tool-rename defines a callable production interface. The approved design specifies only the MCP surface (java_rename arguments/result), while feat-tool-rename is not-started; inventing its module/process contract would violate the Test-Implementer boundary. Resume after feat-tool-rename supplies the callable seam.

features.name: java_code_actions tool
features.behavior: java_code_actions returns available actions as opaque actionId handles bound to the workspace's current sync generation, never round-tripping JDT LS's internal data blob to the caller

context.note: The riskiest v1 item and deliberately last in the build order (docs/design/tool-surface.md#Build-order item 7) — JDT LS returns actions unresolved (edit/command undefined, opaque data blob; spike D), so the daemon must hold that blob server-side, not the caller.

features.falsifier: hands back JDT LS's raw opaque data blob as (or inside) the actionId instead of holding it server-side and minting an opaque handle [INV-CA-2]

features.name: java_apply_code_action tool
features.behavior: java_apply_code_action resolves an actionId's edit via codeAction/resolve only when the workspace's sync generation still matches the one that minted the handle, erroring otherwise

context.note: Shares the code-actions context packet — the staleness hazard (an edit resolved against source that changed since the handle was minted) is the same seam feat-tool-code-actions mints handles against.

features.falsifier: resolves an actionId against source that has changed since the handle was minted instead of erroring [INV-CA-1]

features.name: Prove: a code-action handle is never resolved stale or cross-wired
features.behavior: Minting a handle, editing the file, then resolving it always errors, and a handle table under interleaved calls across two workspaces never resolves one workspace's handle into another's edit

context.note: Interleave calls across two real workspaces deliberately (mint in A, mint in B, resolve A's, resolve B's) — a handle table keyed only by actionId without a workspace tag would pass a single-workspace test and still fail this one.

features.falsifier: resolving a handle after an intervening edit to the same file returns an edit instead of erroring [INV-CA-1]; or a handle minted in one workspace resolves to an edit belonging to the other workspace's action [INV-CA-2]
features.checkerNotes:
BLOCKED: code-action oracle requires callable interfaces owned by two not-started dependencies.

TCON-CA-0001 through TCON-CA-0005 require real java_code_actions mint calls and java_apply_code_action resolve calls, including workspace sync-generation changes and interleaving across two live workspaces. docs/design/tool-surface.md specifies tool arguments and observable semantics, but it does not define an executable/CLI entry point, TypeScript signatures, concrete action/edit/error result shapes, or a fixture contract for producing multiple resolvable actions. feat-tool-code-actions and feat-tool-apply-code-action are both not-started, so writing the integration test now would invent their production interfaces or fail only on missing modules rather than behavior. Implement and specify those dependencies first, then route this proof feature back to test-implementer.

features.name: Prove: the full shim to daemon to real JDT LS pipeline holds together
features.behavior: An agent editing a file directly on disk and then calling a tool through the real shim-to-daemon-to-JDT-LS pipeline on a fixture Maven project always gets a routed, post-edit-or-explicit-resync answer, never a stale one served through a wrong workspace

context.note: Replaces the scaffold's feat-002/feat-003 placeholders: this system has no microservice boundary, but it has the cross-process one (shim <-> daemon <-> JDT LS, docs/design/architecture.md#Feature-impact) that deserves the same integration-level treatment testing-standards.md's Level 3 asks for. Drive it through the real npx-launched shim, not an in-process call.

features.falsifier: the end-to-end pipeline answers a post-edit tool call from the pre-edit model, or answers a call against the wrong workspace's real JDT LS instance [INV-SYNC-1][INV-ROUTE-1]
